risks.title: Margin pressures in Asia due to Chinese OEMs
risks.summary: The rise of low-cost Chinese automakers is exerting increasing pressure on Adient's margins in Asia, despite its efforts to win new contracts.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is cited as leading to modest but continuous margin declines, with high intensity in the text (e.g., 'pricing pressures', 'intensifying competition from Chinese imports'). It is repeated across multiple sections and linked to a structural trend of rising local OEMs in China, reinforcing its severity. The Competition category is heavily weighted here. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Declining automotive demand and overcapacity in EMEA
risks.summary: Weak demand, overcapacity, and increased competition in Europe threaten Adient's profitability and asset valuation in the EMEA region.
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions a €333 million goodwill impairment directly tied to lower expected volumes in EMEA. The language is alarming ('overcapacity', 'pricing pressure', 'intensifying competition'). This risk is central to the asset valuation analysis and exacerbated by significant volume issues in Europe, making it existential for the region. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Impacts of supply chain disruptions
risks.summary: Ongoing disruptions in supply chains continue to affect Adient's production, with unplanned shutdowns and shortages of critical components.
risks.score_rationale: The text highlights persistent disruptions, unplanned stoppages, operational inefficiencies, and an ongoing fragile supply chain. The intensity of the language ('supply chain disruptions', 'shortages of critical components') and direct impact on production justify a high severity rating. The Industrial category is moderately weighted. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Exposure to currency fluctuations
risks.summary: Adient's international operations expose it significantly to exchange rate movements, which its hedging strategies do not fully offset.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly linked to financial results volatility and interperiod comparability. The text mentions hedging policies but emphasizes their insufficiency. The exposure is recurring and affects financial stability as a multinational operating in 29 countries, with high weighting for the Capital category. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on inaccurate customer forecasts
risks.summary: Errors in customer production forecasts can lead to misalignments in Adient's planning and costs.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned as potentially having an 'adverse impact' but without quantified losses. The language is moderate. It is stable year-on-year and linked to a typical operational risk in the automotive sector, with medium weighting for the Industrial category. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Risks related to raw material and energy costs
risks.summary: Persistent inflationary environment on key inputs weighs on Adient's costs, with limited ability to pass through these increases to customers.
risks.score_rationale: The text describes 'significant' volatility in material, energy, freight, and labor prices, with a sustained impact expected into fiscal 2026. The risk directly affects Adient's gross margins (6.6% in 2025 vs 6.3% in 2024) and is repeatedly cited as a key pressure factor, with high weighting for the Macro category. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Russia-Ukraine conflict and economic sanctions
risks.summary: The Ukraine conflict continues to affect supply chains and energy costs, with increased risks for operations in EMEA.
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions impacts on energy costs, supply chains, and geopolitical uncertainties. Although Adient no longer has operations in Russia, its suppliers and customers are affected. The language emphasizes risks ('geopolitical uncertainties', 'impact on supply chain'), and the Ukraine conflict continues to affect the EMEA region, with high weighting for Geopolitical.
